title: Clarify ephemeral proxy-key origin resolution for subproject usage attribution
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary:

Some customers are seeing bursts of usage billed to the parent org/project after ephemeral proxy-keys (short-lived tokens minted by our SDKs/agents for subprojects) are rotated or re-exchanged via the gateway. Symptoms include incorrect billing attribution, quota eviction against the parent project, and unexpected rate-limit enforcement for the wrong workspace. This ticket scopes diagnosis and fixes for the attribution logic used during transient key handoffs and token-exchange flows.

Observed behaviour:
- SDKs mint ephemeral proxy-keys tied to a subproject alias; these are exchanged at edge proxies with a short TTL. During edge-proxy rotation and certain proxy failovers we observed that requests in flight fall back to a legacy claim-resolution path that resolves caller->parent org instead of subproject.
- Misattribution window appears concentrated around: key rotate (gateway rolling deploy), proxy restart, and stale claim-cache reads (~5-30s).
- Affected systems: billing metering (per-project tokens), rate-limiter attribution (global counters), usage analytics.

Metrics / evidence:
- Customer-reported billing spike: org-1209 (internal report) on 2026-01-31; ingestion trace shows 22k token requests labeled parent-org:acct-1209 within a 90s window coincident with an edge deploy.
- Rate-limiter logs show counters incremented against parent project id for tokens whose original issuer claim included subproject alias header.
- KV claim-cache TTL was set to 15s on the problematic fleet; repro against staging with TTL=1s increases incidence.

Root cause hypothesis:
1) During token-exchange, the gateway attempts to resolve a canonical owner via a two-step: local claim-cache lookup -> fallback to lookup-by-integration-token. If cache returns stale/missing entries while the token has a newer subproject binding, the fallback path resolves to a parent mapping that predates the subproject alias.
2) The exchange path does not cryptographically bind the ephemeral proxy-key to the subproject namespace; therefore, when the cache is missing, the system accepts a looser mapping.
3) Some proxies perform a best-effort repair (re-mint) and retry without preserving the original subproject claim, causing downstream services to record the parent org.

Proposed fix (phased):
Phase A (short-term, low-risk)
- Change attribution fallback to be strict: if claim-cache is missing, reject attribution to parent and mark request as "attribution-unknown" for downstream systems. This avoids incorrect billing but will surface rejected requests; we will credit back known-customer hits later via reconciliation.
- Instrument and add an alert for attribution-unknown rate > X per minute per region.

Phase B (medium-term)
- Modify token-exchange API to include an origin binding field (opaque audit-hash derived from subproject id + key id) signed by gateway. Downstream components will prefer signed binding over legacy lookup.
- Add atomic update to claim-cache during successful exchange to prevent transient misses during rolling deploys.

Phase C (long-term)
- Backfill re-attribution job: for the reconciliation window (configurable, default 7 days) attempt to re-map previously recorded attribution-unknown entries to the canonical subproject by replaying exchange proofs and request traces. Create billing-adjustment pipeline for affected customers.

Implementation notes / trade-offs:
- Phase A changes are low-risk but create false-negatives (requests marked unknown). We will need a temporary customer communication plan and credits path.
- Phase B requires changes to multiple components (gateway, claim-cache, rate-limiter, billing-ingest) and an update to our SDKs to propagate the signed binding for edge replays. This is more invasive but reduces future ambiguity.
- Phase C is operationally heavy (forensics + billing adjustments) but necessary to restore retroactive accuracy and customer trust.

Acceptance criteria:
- No new requests get misattributed to parent org in new incidents after Phase B rollout (0 occurrences in production for 24h during a rolling deploy stress run).
- Attribution-unknown is under 0.1% of total requests in peak traffic post-Phase A and decays after Phase B.

2026-02-20 Maya Patel: PM note - notify affected customers of credit path if we enable Phase A in prod. Coordinate with billing ops. Also flagged as P0 for potential customer charge-impact.

2026-03-01 Infrastructure: rolling-window analysis shows claim-cache TTL variance across fleets. Action: standardize to atomic compare-swap writes during exchange (required for Phase B).
2026-03-03 Design review: discussed UX for reporting attribution-unknown to customers (billing portal flag + transient credit). Approved messaging copy.
